item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers have an unfortunate history of late-season injuries preceding postseason runs. September injuries to Christian Yelich and Brandon Woodruff are the most recent examples, but the trend also extends to Devin Williams breaking his hand after punching a wall in 2021, Ben Sheets not being a part of the 2008 postseason run after a flexor tendon injury, and of course, Rollie Fingers' forearm injury ahead of the team's memorable 1982 run.
With just over 24 hours remaining until the Brewers' 2026 postseason opener, this year's team thankfully hasn't made a contribution to that disheartening list. However, as the Brewers finish out their stretch of five days off -- the result of them earning a first-round bye -- there was an injury scare that had Brewers fans feeling déjà vu.
Infielder Joey Ortiz exited the Brewers' Friday night opener in their final series of the regular season with a noticeable limp. After the game, manager Pat Murphy revealed that Ortiz had been battling soreness in his knee due to a bruise he sustained during the team's series against the Philadelphia Phillies and also some inflammation in his abdomen that has been causing him discomfort.
Ortiz didn't play either of the final two games of the regular season, and his postseason roster status was briefly in doubt when Murphy couldn't commit one way or another on Tuesday afternoon. However, thankfully, during Friday's media availability, the Brewers' manager took a more optimistic tone when talking about his injured infielder. Said Murphy on Ortiz on Friday afternoon, "It looks like it's progressing in the right direction...I would say at this point we're planning on him being available."
The Brewers are planning on Joey Ortiz "being available" for the NLDS
Despite his struggles during the 2025 season and first half of the 2026 campaign, Ortiz became one of the Brewers' most productive hitters during the second half of this year. In fact, Ortiz had the ninth best OPS (.883) among NL hitters with at least 200 plate appearances, from July 1 to the end of the season. As crazy as the statement would have sounded during the middle of May, Ortiz is one of the Brewers' key offensive X-factors heading into the postseason.
Therefore, it would have been a significant blow had Ortiz missed out on the 2026 postseason run due to his late-season knee and abdomen injuries, but thankfully the Brewers' infielder is expected to be available tomorrow night.
Ortiz's production would indicate that he should start every game regardless of the handedness of the opposing pitcher, but Murphy consistently used David Hamilton against tough right-handed starters at third base, so it's not yet certain just how many games Joey O will start in the postseason. That said, the Padres just announced that southpaw Robbie Ray is getting the ball in Game 1, so Ortiz will almost certainly be manning the hot corner on Saturday night. Regardless of how many at-bats Murphy gives his surging third baseman in October, it's undeniably a welcome development that Ortiz will likely be available for the NLDS roster.

item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers have received encouraging news about Andrew Vaughn ahead of their National League Division Series against the San Diego Padres. However, Joey Ortiz’s situation is a little more complicated as the team prepares for its postseason opener.
Manager Pat Murphy provided updates on both infielders, giving Milwaukee a clearer picture of its available options heading into the series.
According to David Gasper of Brewers Daily, Vaughn is a full go this week after overcoming an illness that sidelined him. The first baseman is expected to be available as the Brewers prepare for their matchup with San Diego.
That is an encouraging development for Milwaukee, which will want its regular lineup available against a Padres team coming off a Wild Card sweep.
Joey Ortiz Remains Limited Ahead of Brewers’ Postseason Opener
Ortiz’s update was more cautious. Murphy said the infielder’s MRI results were clear, but he will remain a little limited in high-intensity activities ahead of Game 1.
The third baseman has been dealing with a bruised right knee and abdominal swelling. While the imaging results offer some reassurance, his activity restrictions leave questions about how much he can contribute immediately.
Here’s Murphy’s update on Ortiz, shared by Gasper:
Pat Murphy on Joey Ortiz: His MRI results were clear, but he remains a little limited in high-intensity activities as he deals with a bruised right knee and abdominal swelling.
Ortiz’s availability matters because Milwaukee will need to manage its infield carefully if he cannot handle his usual workload. The Brewers will have to monitor his condition as they approach the opening game.
Vaughn’s expected availability gives the team some positive news, but Ortiz’s situation remains worth watching. Milwaukee now has a better idea of what to expect from two important infielders, although the final picture will depend on Ortiz’s progress before the series begins.
The Brewers will hope both players can contribute as they prepare for a challenging postseason matchup.

item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers don't have to reveal their National League Division Series roster until Saturday morning, but the organization gave a positive update on Friday ahead of the official announcement.
Throughout the week, the guy to watch from an injury perspective has been infielder Joey Ortiz. The 28-year-old has been dealing with knee and abdominal injuries, but is trending in the right direction. Brewers manager Pat Murphy said so himself on Friday and noted that the expectation is that he will be good to go for the National League Division Series.
"It looks like it's progressing in the right direction," Murphy said. "He's still ... he still has some pain. He's going to tell you, 'no,' and all that kind of stuff. He wants to play very badly. I would say at this point, we are planning on him being available."
Joey Ortiz Is Going To Be Alright
There was a point during the 2026 season in which this update wouldn't have moved the needle much for Milwaukee. But things are certainly different now. Before he shifted from shortstop to third base, Ortiz was really struggling offensively. He was batting .207 with one home run and 14 RBIs in 60 games before Cooper Pratt made his big league debut. Pratt made his debut on June 16, which shifted Ortiz's role away from shortstop.
Things changed for the better for Ortiz afterward. From June 17 through the end of the season, Ortiz slashed .310/.348/.491 with an .840 OPS, eight home runs, 33 RBIs, nine doubles and four triples in 74 games.
He went from being someone at risk of being sent down to the minors, to being integral to this club's success down the stretch. Fortunately, when the Brewers open up National League Division Series play on Saturday, the current expectation is that Ortiz will be in the mix, barring some sort of last-second setback.
The Brewers have a tough series ahead. The San Diego Padres are the hottest team in baseball and aren't going to be an easy out. For the Brewers to win, they're going to need all of the help that they can get. So, this update is very positive for the organization heading into their most important series of the season so far. If the Brewers can take down the Padres in the NLDS, they would advance to face either the Los Angeles Dodgers or the Atlanta Braves in the National League Championship Series.

item.content:encoded:
Pat Murphy provided an update on Joey Ortiz as the Milwaukee Brewers prepare for their National League Division Series opener.
Ortiz underwent an MRI over the weekend, with Murphy saying the structural results were good. However, the Brewers manager remains cautious because Ortiz is dealing with a bruised right knee and abdominal swelling.
Ortiz has not played since leaving Milwaukee's Sept. 25 game against the St. Louis Cardinals in the eighth inning.
Brewers Manager Pat Murphy said Andrew Vaughn is a full go this week, but they are still keeping an eye on Joey Ortiz’s abdomen and knee.
Murphy says Ortiz will be a “little limited” and they are keeping him from some of the higher intensity activities in today’s workout.
The Brewers have extra time to monitor Ortiz because their 103-59 regular season earned them a first-round bye. Milwaukee will open the NLDS on Oct. 3 against the winner of the Chicago Cubs and San Diego Padres Wild Card Series.
Ortiz was an important part of the Brewers' infield during the regular season. He appeared in 134 games and hit .270 with a .328 on-base percentage, .402 slugging percentage, nine home runs, 47 RBI and nine stolen bases.
Ortiz also recorded 100 hits, 14 doubles and four triples while drawing 35 walks. His availability could give Milwaukee another option in the infield as the team begins its postseason run.
For now, Murphy is giving Ortiz time rather than rushing him back into game action. The seven-day window between his last regular-season appearance and the NLDS gives the Brewers additional time to evaluate his condition.
Milwaukee enters October after winning 103 games, but Ortiz's health is one of the situations the team will continue monitoring before Game 1. His status should become clearer as the Brewers get closer to their postseason opener.

item.content:encoded:
Brewers record their first 100-win season with victory over Phillies
The Milwaukee Brewers reached 100 wins for the first time, and Jackson Chourio hit his 25th homer to lift them to a 5-1 victory over Philadelphia on Thursday night that slowed the Phillies’ playoff push.
The Phillies needed a win to at least have a shot at clinching their fifth straight trip to the playoffs. They instead can try again to clinch for the third straight game on Friday against Tampa Bay.
Philadelphia played without NL batting leader Luis Arraez after he came off with a sprained left ankle after he tried to avoid a tag at first base.
Milwaukee reached one more milestone to go with its National League Central title and a first-round postseason bye. The Brewers are the first team this year to reach 100 wins and are trying to hold off the defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers for the No. 1 seed in the NL playoffs. Their previous high was 97 wins last year.
Brewers fans crowded the seats behind the dugout and held “100” signs as players left the field.
Bryce Harper tied the game 1-1 with an RBI single in the third.
Jake Bauers hit the tie-breaking single off José Alvarado (5-4) in the eighth inning, and Cooper Pratt and Joey Ortiz added run-scoring singles in the inning for a 4-1 lead. Chourio hit a solo shot in the ninth.
JoJo Romero (3-3) got the win and Antonio Senzatela earned his fourth save.
Phillies starter Andrew Painter had another terrific outing in a second-half rebound that should see him play a role in the postseason in the rotation or out of the bullpen. He allowed Sam Frelick’s RBI double in the second and finished with eight strikeouts and three walks in six innings.
The rookie right-hander was demoted to the minors in June after a 12-4 loss to Miami left him with eight losses in nine decisions and a 7.06 ERA. Since his July 31 recalled has a 3.65 ERA in 11 starts with 62 strikeouts to 23 walks.
Philadelphia got more good pitching news earlier in the day when All-Star lefty Jesús Luzardo said he has recovered enough from left shoulder inflammation that he should be able to pitch next week in the playoffs.
Up next
Milwaukee tunes up for the playoffs with a three-game homestand against St. Louis.

item.content:encoded:
Brewers take down Phillies for franchise's first 100-win season
(Photo credit: Bill Streicher)
Jake Bauers' RBI single in the eighth inning plated the go-ahead run Thursday for the Milwaukee Brewers, who reached the 100-win mark for the first time in franchise history with their 5-1 win over the hosting Philadelphia Phillies.
Bauers, who went 2-for-5 and added a double, singled up the middle, allowing Jackson Chourio to score from second, giving the Brewers (100-59) a 2-1 lead and starting a three-run frame. Chourio, who pinch-hit for designated hitter William Contreras, led off the frame with a walk off Jose Alvarado (5-4) and stole second.
Gary Sanchez singled deep to left field to put runners on the corners, and after Alvarado got Luis Lara to line out to shallow center, Cooper Pratt (2-for-3) welcomed Chase Shugart with another hit up the middle to give the Brewers a two-run lead. Joey Ortiz added a two-out hit, a blooper to shallow center that allowed Sanchez to score from second.
Chourio added a solo home run, his 25th blast of the season, in the ninth.
Five Brewers pitchers held the Phillies (87-72) to just four hits. JoJo Romero (3-3) allowed one hit in 1 1/3 innings against St. Louis, who Milwaukee acquired him from last month. Romero picked up his second win with the Brewers since coming off the injured list (appendectomy) earlier this month.
Antonio Senzatela relieved Romero, allowing a walk over the final 1 2/3 innings to earn his fourth save.
Phillies starter Andrew Painter held the Brewers to just one run over six innings. The rookie allowed five hits and three walks while matching a season-high eight strikeouts. His only blemish came in the second, when Sal Frelick doubled home Sanchez.
Kyle Schwarber (2-for-4) and Bryce Harper (2-for-4) combined to get all four of the Phillies hits. Harper's third-inning single scored Schwarber, who led off the frame with a double off Brewers starter Shane Drohan. Philadelphia managed just one hit, a Schwarber single in the seventh, against the Brewers bullpen.
Besides losing the game, the Phillies may also have lost infielder Luis Arraez, who reportedly sprained an ankle trying to avoid a tag on a groundout in the sixth inning.
With the win, Milwaukee can officially clinch home-field advantage throughout the postseason should the Los Angeles Dodgers lose Thursday night to the visiting San Diego Padres.
Philadelphia remains in an NL wild-card spot, but the Phillies could not drop their magic number to clinch from two.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
When the Milwaukee Brewers faced off against the Philadelphia Phillies on Tuesday night, they didn't have third baseman Joey Ortiz in the lineup.
Ortiz is someone who has had a roller coaster of a season, to say the least. He spent the first few months at shortstop and was very good defensively, but really struggled offensively. At the time, it was talked about how Cooper Pratt would be coming at some point and that would be bad news for Ortiz's role. When Pratt did arrive, Ortiz moved to third base. At the time, his bat also came alive.
He has turned his season around and he has become a key cog in this lineup, which at one point was very unexpected. But he wasn't in the lineup on Tuesday against the righty Zack Wheeler. Is that something Brewers fans should expect in the playoffs? Brewers manager Pat Murphy broke down that very question, as shared on X by MLB.com's Adam McCalvy.
"Joey doesn't work as well versus that two-seamer, but if it was the playoffs today, Joey would be in there," Murphy said. "He's been so good for us, and I don't want to waver his confidence at all. But he's got a little abdominal strain thing going on that he's been fighting. I noticed a little bit of it a couple of days ago. We're looking to get him a break. And we need to get [David Hamilton] in there. Same with [Luis Lara]. I would probably start [Sal Frelick] today, but we have to get Lara some at-bats against right-handers, too."
Joey Ortiz Will Help Milwaukee
This is an intriguing insight into how the club is viewing the playoff lineup already. Earlier in the season, there was more of a committee at third base. Ortiz and Hamilton both got a chunk of time, but Ortiz really has turned around his season to the point that he deserves to be the main guy.
Ortiz has played in 131 games so far this season and is slashing .267/.326/.403 with a .729 OPS, nine home runs, 46 RBIs, nine stolen bases, 14 doubles, four triples and 49 runs scored. Plus, on top of his elite defense, he doesn't strike out. Ortiz has struck out just 78 times in his 131 games played.
When it comes to the Phillies, they are realistically a team Milwaukee could face in the National League Division Series. If the season were to end today, the Phillies would face the Chicago Cubs in the Wild Card round with the winner of the three-game series heading to face Milwaukee.
If the Brewers and the Phillies face off in the playoffs, Milwaukee will very likely see Wheeler again and it sounds like the lineup would look different, especially with Ortiz. Murphy noted that he would probably start Sal Frelick in a playoff game in this scenario as well.
It may have just been a regular season game on a Tuesday. But we did get some valuable insights into how this club is viewing the lineup heading into the postseason.

A falta de una semana para que termine la temporada regular en la MLB, el panorama de playoffs comienza a definirse y con ello te presentamos aquellos peloteros mexicanos que ya aseguraron su clasificación a playoffs y quienes todavía están en la pelea por entrar a la postemporada.
Mexicanos que ya aseguraron su pase a postemporada
La presencia de peloteros mexicanos en las últimas ediciones de los playoffs ha sido constante y este año no será la excepción pues hasta ahorita se tiene confirmada la participación de cuatro peloteros mexicanos y dos con estatus todavía pendiente, ya que uno está en sucursales y el otro se encuentra en lista de lesionados.
PUBLICIDAD
A continuación, te presentamos la lista de jugadores nacionales que estarán en los playoffs:
Jonathan Aranda (Tampa Bay Rays)
Ha firmado su campaña más sólida y consagratoria en MLB. Con 149 juegos jugados, el infielder presume un promedio de bateo de .277, conectando 156 imparables, 22 cuadrangulares y remolcando 92 carreras, convirtiéndose en una pieza medular en el lineup de los Rays.
Jarren Durán (Boston Red Sox):
Se ha consolidado como un auténtico motor en los senderos y el jardín central. A lo largo de la temporada suma 20 jonrones, 69 carreras impulsadas y 19 bases robadas en 145 encuentros, destacando además por su velocidad con 5 triples.
PUBLICIDAD
Joey Ortiz (Milwaukee Brewers):
Ha sido una de las grandes revelaciones del año tras su llegada a Milwaukee, aportando una defensa de élite en el cuadro y un bateo sumamente oportuno que ayudó a los Brewers a amarrar temprano su boleto a octubre.
Patrick Sandoval (Boston Red Sox):
El lanzador que representó a México en el Clásico Mundial de Beisbol regresó esta temporada tras un periodo largo fuera de las canchas y ha tenido altibajos con los Boston Red Sox con una efectividad de 5.15 y un récord de 1-7.
Manuel Rodríguez (Tampa Bay Rays):
El lanzador yucateco venía sumando valiosos relevos con efectividad de 3.86 y 8 ponches en el bullpen de Tampa Bay en los cuatro juegos que disputó.
PUBLICIDAD
No obstante, Manuel Rodríguez se encuentra actualmente en la lista de lesionados (IL) de 15 días debido a una distensión en la espalda baja (low back strain), por lo que el cuerpo técnico espera su evolución para ver si podrá estar listo en las primeras rondas de los playoffs.
Alek Thomas (Oklahoma City Comets):
Después de haber sido cambiado desde los Arizona Diamondbacks a inicios de año, el jardinero Alek Thomas se encuentra actualmente en las sucursales de Los Angeles Dodgers
Aunque tuvo una breve participación de 7 juegos con el primer equipo de los Dodgers bateando para .211, la tremenda profundidad del roster angelino ha hecho que se mantenga buscando ritmo en el sistema de ligas menores, a la espera de un llamado que lo devuelva al roster de postemporada.
PUBLICIDAD
Peloteros mexicanos todavía buscan entrar a la postemporada
La presencia de peloteros mexicanos aumentará conforme avance la semana, con varios representantes en equipos que continúan en competencia por buscar entrar a los playoffs.
Toronto Blue Jays cuenta con Alejandro Kirk, Tibo Rodríguez, Brandon Valenzuela y Luis Urías. Por su parte, Randy Arozarena y Andrés Muñoz forman parte de los Seattle Mariners.
Isaac Paredes representa a los Houston Astros, mientras Javier Assad se encuentra con los Chicago Cubs. Alejandro Osuna integra el roster de los Texas Rangers.
Taijuan Walker juega con los Philadelphia Phillies y Jeremiah Estrada pertenece a los San Diego Padres.
Cada uno luchará hasta el último segundo por entrar a la postemporada.

item.content:encoded:
The Yankees’ odds of winning the AL East are down to 2.8 percent per FanGraphs after getting walked off by the Diamondbacks last night. I know mathematically that makes sense, but the chances mentally feel even more extreme. I’ve been having “fun” (or whatever) comping the odds to certain pitchers from history getting a hit. We are the dregs. Remember mid-2000s Mets pitcher Aaron Heilman? I personally remember him most for giving up the homer to Yadier Molina late in Game 7 of the 2006 NLCS, just before Adam Wainwright famously caught Carlos Beltrán looking to win the pennant.
Anyway, Heilman was a horrendous hitter. He singled once in his rookie year, and then never got another hit. He ended his career 1-for-47, so an .021 average. So the Yankees just need magic only a little bit more sufficient than that RBI single by Heilman off Sidney Ponson on August 12, 2003! Hell yeah.
It’s not happening, but we press on because it’s good to check up on what everyone else is doing anyway. Here’s what was going on Saturday.
Tampa Bay Rays (94-60) 2, Boston Red Sox (84-71) 1
The Yankees gained a full game on the Rays on Friday for the first time in over a week, as Boston snapped their six-game winning streak. There was no such fortune to be found yesterday though; Tampa Bay made sure of that well before first pitch in Arizona, and it only got worse from there. By the end of the night, the Rays once again had a five-game lead over the Yanks; Tampa Bay’s magic number (combination of Rays wins or Yankees losses) to clinch the AL East is four.
This one was a pitchers’ duel to the bitter end. Brayan Bello had easily his best outing of a turbulent season (and probably the best of his career), firing eight shutout frames at the Trop and fanning 11 Rays, tying a personal best from July 9, 2024. As he only went 5.1 in that one and faced merely the soon-to-depart-Oakland A’s rather than the division-leading Rays.
The only true blemish on Bello’s record came when Jonathan Aranda cracked an opposite-field homer to make it a 1-1 game in the fourth. Tampa Bay had a chance to make it 2-1 against Bello in the seventh when Liam Hicks and Chandler Simpson led off with singles. Bello then induced a grounder from Victor Mesa Jr. to move up the runners, and then another off the bat of Richie Palacios to Trevor Story, who nailed pinch-runner Jonny DeLuca at home. Palacios swiped second, but Bello fanned Cedric Mullins to end the inning. The Rays went down in order in the eighth to end Bello’s brilliant night.
Unfortunately for Bello, a win wasn’t in the cards because Boston put up next to nothing against Freddy Peralta and the Rays’ pitching staff. Doubles by Caleb Durbin and Roman Anthony gave the Red Sox their one run in the second, but they were stymied from there. They had chances!
- Second inning after Anthony’s two-out double: Mickey Gasper lineout to center
- Fourth inning with runners on first and second, one out: Story strikeout, Durbin popout
- Fifth inning with runner on second, one out: Anthony groundout, Gasper strikeout
- Sixth inning with runners on first and second, two out: Durbin fly out to left
- Eighth inning after Adley Rutschman’s one-out double: Wilyer Abreu strikeout, Nick Sogard lineout
Even against lockdown Rays closer Bryan Baker, Boston had one last shot to take a late lead. After Story grounded out, Durbin lined a double down the left field line to put himself in scoring position for Jarren Duran. Durbin darted from second, however, and got thrown out stealing third. Duran promptly followed with a triple over DeLuca’s head in center. Isiah Kiner-Falefa bounced one to Junior Caminero at third to end the threat.
Granted a chance to walk it off, Tampa Bay didn’t waste it. Rather than blasting a homer to finish the game as he had twice earlier this homestand, Caminero began the ninth against Garrett Whitlock with a single to left. (A catwalk curtailed Durbin’s effort to catch a popup earlier in the AB.) DeLuca popped up, but Chandler Simpson grounded one through the six-hole for another hit. The runners moved up when catcher Connor Wong let a Whitlock sinker up bounce off his glove for a passed ball. Palacios ended the night with flare to center that fell in, securing the win for Tampa Bay. At least the Wild Card Series is also almost certainly going to be at Yankee Stadium now, I suppose.
AL Rock Fight
Cleveland Guardians (80-75) 12, The Athletics (61-94) 6
Two crooked numbers effectively decided Saturday’s affair with the A’s in a hurry. Tanner Bibee kind of stunk and would allow six runs in a dozen hits while failing to make through five, but it hardly mattered. Cleveland erased a 2-0 deficit in the first on a three-run shot from rookie Chase DeLauter and two-run homer by Angel Martinez. The A’s got one back in the third, only to see another five-spot from the Guardians on poor Jacob Lopez as David Fry, Austin Hedges, and Brayan Rocchio all delivered RBI doubles. Martinez later added a homer and an RBI single in a career-best four-hit day.
Chicago White Sox (79-76) 3, Detroit Tigers (73-82) 1
Cleveland’s win meant that Chicago was stuck at a game back in the AL Central in the best-case, but they did at least help push one of their Wild Card foes out of the picture with a win. Honestly, this was probably kind of a dud of a game for anyone who isn’t a White Sox fan, the lone highlights being Sean Burke’s six scoreless frames and Miguel Vargas’ sixth-inning solo shot to make it 3-1, Chicago (the other runs scored on an RBI single by Munetaka Murakami and a fifth-inning sac fly). Spencer Torkelson had a chance to tie the game with a homer following Hao-Yu Lee’s two-out single in the ninth, but he flew out to center to end it.
Milwaukee Brewers (97-58) 1, Baltimore Orioles (75-80) 0
Yeah, it’s time to stick a fork in the O’s. It was all but certain for awhile now, but Chicago’s win combined with Baltimore’s second-straight loss to Milwaukee means that the Orioles are four back with a week to play, plus multiple teams in front of them. Trevor Rogers was the hard-luck loser here while Baltimore got blanked on four hits and Rece Hinds lost a fly ball from Joey Ortiz in the sun, allowing him to triple and score on Gary Sánchez’s RBI grounder. Woof.
Texas Rangers (78-77) 6, Toronto Blue Jays (76-79) 1
The O’s aren’t the only bird that are all but shot down, either. Trade Deadline acquisition José Soriano coughed up an early homer to Josh Jung, beginning a five-inning, six-run outing that pushed Toronto three games out in the Wild Card and the Rangers into a one-game AL West lead over Houston. The only downside for Texas was that second-half surprise Cal Quantrill—who has a 1.75 ERA since re-entering the rotation in late July—left in the second with lat tightness, so old friend Jordan Montgomery picked up the slack in long relief, retiring 11 of the 12 hitters he faced with no hits allowed.
Atlanta Braves (91-64) 6, Houston Astros (77-78) 3
Houston and Texas have been wrestling all week over the prestigious “Who can win this horri-awful division with a .500-ish record” crown. Sunday it went to Texas with the Astros falling out of their tie for first place (remember that they own the tiebreaker). Isaac Paredes had put Houston ahead with a solo homer and an RBI knock in the third, but the Astros’ bullpen set that lead on fire. The big blow came off the bat of Ronald Acuña Jr., who belted a grand slam off Bryan Abreu in the seventh after AJ Blubaugh made a right mess of things.

item.content:encoded:
BALTIMORE (AP) — The Milwaukee Brewers tied a team record with their 97th win of the season, beating Baltimore 1-0 Saturday with the help of a fly ball lost in the sun by Orioles right fielder Rece Hinds.
Already assured of their fourth straight NL Central title and eighth playoff berth in nine season, the big league-best Brewers (97-58) matched the wins total of last year’s team that finished 97-65.
Baltimore (75-80) fell four games behind the Chicago White Sox for the AL’s last wild card with seven to play.
Robert Gasser (5-5) allowed three hits over seven innings, Abner Uribe worked around a leadoff single in the eighth, and Aaron Ashby pitched a perfect ninth for his third save, finishing the Brewers’ 11th shutout this season and first 1-0 win.
Hinds lost Joey Ortiz’s fly ball in the sun in the second inning and tumbled to the ground, and Gary Sánchez hit into a run-scoring groundout.
Trevor Rogers (10-11) struck out 10, walked one and allowed three hits in a season-high eight innings.
Up next
Milwaukee RHP Jacob Misiorowski (15-5, 1.89 ERA) faces Baltimore RHP Brandon Young (9-4, 3.65) as the three-game series concludes Sunday night.

item.content:encoded:
The Milwaukee Brewers are nearing the end of the MLB regular season. They defeated the Baltimore Orioles 6-5 Friday night, with Jackson Chourio driving in three runs. Prior to Game 2, the team announced news regarding Christian Yelich.
Saturday's game will feature a pitching battle between Robert Gasser and Trevor Rogers. The game will be broadcast at 3:05 PM Central Time, 4:05 PM Eastern Time. The Brewers are 8-2 in their last 10 contests, while the Orioles are 6-4.
Milwaukee Brewers Announce Big Christian Yelich News During Baltimore Orioles Series
Prior to the first pitch of their second game against the Orioles, the Brewers announced lineup news. For Yelich fans, the news is especially important.
- LF: Jackson Chourio
- 1B: Vaughn
- C: Gary Sanchez
- SS: Cooper Pratt
- RF: Luis Lara
- 2B: David Hamilton
Starting Pitcher: Robert Gasser.
Judging from the roster for today's game, Gary Sanchez is coming in while Yelich comes out. William Contreras moves to designated hitter to make room for Sanchez.
Yelich is a 34-year-old slugger, while Sanchez is a 33-year-old catcher for the Brewers.
Looking At Christian Yelich & Gary Sanchez
Yelich is a 14-year MLB veteran who has been with the Brewers for nine seasons.
Over his career, he has been an All-Star several times, culminating in an NL MVP award in 2018. Yelich has enjoyed a solid 2026 campaign, notching 101 hits, 57 RBIs, 11 stolen bases, and 11 home runs in 112 games.
On the other hand, Sanchez has 44 hits, 35 RBIs, and 11 home runs in 83 games.
Pat Murphy on Christian Yelich
Recently, the Brewers manager has discussed Yelich's work ethic and his dedication to the game.
"I just remember he was here one night till 1 o'clock in the morning. A lot of guys in his situation, you've won MVP, you've been an all-star multiple times, you've done all the things in the game, you are 12 years in your career, and you know what: he still cares so much about the Milwaukee Brewers. That's the beauty of this whole thing…you have no idea how much this guy cares," Murphy said via a social media clip from Hunter Baumgardt.
Brewers Manager Pat Murphy reflects on a night during Christian Yelich’s tough stretch that Yeli was at the park working till 1:00am and how his care for the Milwaukee Brewers has led to him to getting back on track👇
“That’s the beauty of this whole thing.” pic.twitter.com/FkQGDmDkPJ
— Hunter Baumgardt (@hunterbonair) August 30, 2026
Whether Yelich is in the lineup or taking a night off to stay healthy for a deep playoff run, it sounds like Brewers fans are lucky to have him.
